P000.title: Unexpected server error
P000.message: Something went wrong on the server
P000.meaning: The server hit an error it has no specific code for.
P000.fix: Check Admin → Logs (or `docker logs plinthio`) for the full error. Admins also see the cause in the error message itself.

P001.title: Invalid request
P001.meaning: A required field was missing or a value was out of range.
P001.fix: The message says which field. If the web app sent it, reload the page. An old cached version can send outdated requests.

P002.title: Not found
P002.meaning: The thing asked for does not exist, or is hidden from this account.
P002.fix: It may have been deleted or moved by a rescan. Refresh the page.

P003.title: Not allowed
P003.message: You do not have permission to do that
P003.meaning: The account is signed in but not permitted to perform this action.
P003.fix: Ask an admin to change your role or access if you need this.

P004.title: Conflict
P004.message: That conflicts with something that already exists
P004.meaning: The action clashes with existing data, such as a duplicate name.
P004.fix: The message says what clashed. Rename or remove the existing item first.

P005.title: Too many requests
P005.message: Too many requests, slow down and try again shortly
P005.fix: Wait a minute and try again. If many people share one IP behind a reverse proxy, set TRUST_PROXY=1 so they are limited separately.

P006.title: Temporarily unavailable
P006.message: The server is busy, try again shortly
P006.meaning: The server could not handle the request right now.
P006.fix: Try again in a few seconds.

P007.title: Upload rejected
P007.message: That file could not be uploaded
P007.meaning: An uploaded file was too large or of the wrong type.
P007.fix: Images must be under 15 MB. Backups must be Plinthio backup files.

P100.title: Sign-in required
P100.meaning: The request carried no session, media token or API key.
P100.fix: Sign in again. For scripts, send an X-API-Key header.

P101.title: Session expired
P101.message: Session expired, please log in again
P101.meaning: The session token is expired, malformed, or was revoked by a password change or "sign out everywhere".

P102.title: Token used in the wrong place
P102.message: This token is not valid here
P102.meaning: A media token was sent as an Authorization header, or used outside /api/media. Or a session token was put in a URL. Media tokens only work as ?token= on media URLs, and session tokens only work in the Authorization header.
P102.fix: This is a bug in the client that made the request. In the web app, reload the page. If it persists, report it with this code.

P103.title: Account expired
P103.message: Your account access has expired. Please contact your administrator.
P103.meaning: The account has an expiry date that has passed.
P103.fix: An admin can extend or clear the expiry in Admin → Users.

P104.title: Invalid API key
P104.meaning: The X-API-Key (or HTTP Basic password) does not match any key.
P104.fix: Create a new key in Settings → Apps & API keys. Keys are shown only once, when created.

P105.title: Admin only
P105.meaning: This action needs the admin role.
P105.fix: Ask an admin to do it, or to promote your account.

P106.title: Editor or admin only
P106.meaning: This action needs the editor or admin role.
P106.fix: Ask an admin to make your account an editor.

P107.title: Wrong username or password
P107.meaning: The sign-in details did not match an account.
P107.fix: Check the username and password. An admin can reset a password in Admin → Users.

P108.title: Too many sign-in attempts
P108.message: Too many sign-in attempts, try again later
P108.meaning: Sign-in is rate limited to slow down password guessing.

P109.title: Not available away from home
P109.message: This server can only be used from its home network
P109.meaning: The request came from outside the home network (not a home or Tailscale address), and the server only allows home access.
P109.fix: Use Plinthio at home, or through Tailscale. An admin can allow outside access in Admin → Network.

P110.title: This account is for home use only
P110.message: This account can only be used from the home network
P110.meaning: The server allows outside access, but not for this account.
P110.fix: Use Plinthio at home, or ask an admin to allow this account away from home (Admin → Users).

P111.title: Wrong two-factor code
P111.message: That code is not right, or has already been used
P111.meaning: The six-digit code (or backup code) did not match. Codes change every 30 seconds and each works once.
P111.fix: Enter the current code from your authenticator app. Check the phone's clock is set automatically. Lost the phone? Use a backup code, or ask an admin to reset two-factor.

P112.title: Two-factor needed away from home
P112.message: Signing in from outside the home network needs two-factor, which this account has not set up
P112.meaning: The server requires two-factor for sign-ins from outside the home network.
P112.fix: Sign in at home once and turn on two-factor in Settings → Security.

P113.title: Sign-in step expired
P113.message: That sign-in took too long, start again
P113.meaning: The two-factor step of a sign-in has a few minutes to complete, or too many wrong codes were entered.
P113.fix: Enter your username and password again.

P200.title: Library folder not found
P200.meaning: The folder a library points at does not exist inside the server (or container).
P200.fix: In Docker, your media is mounted at /media, so library paths look like /media/Movies. Check MEDIA_DIR in docker/.env points at the right host folder.

P201.title: Library folder unreadable (I/O error)
P201.message: The media folder could not be read (I/O error)
P201.meaning: Reading the folder failed with EIO. Almost always the drive behind it disconnected or was remounted, leaving a stale mount. A remounted USB drive can come back under a new path such as /media/you/Drive1.
P201.fix: Check the drive is connected and mounted (`mount | grep media`). Point MEDIA_DIR at its current mount path and recreate the container. Mounting the drive by UUID in /etc/fstab keeps the path stable.

P202.title: Library folder permission denied
P202.message: The server does not have permission to read that folder
P202.meaning: The folder exists but the Plinthio process cannot read it (EACCES).
P202.fix: Give the container user read access to the media folder, e.g. with `chmod -R o+rX` on the host folder or matching PUID/PGID.

P203.title: Not a folder
P203.message: That path is not a folder
P203.meaning: The library path points at a file rather than a directory.
P203.fix: Choose the folder that contains your media.

P300.title: Media not found
P300.meaning: No item with that id exists, or it is hidden from this account by an admin or parental controls.
P300.fix: Refresh the library. A rescan may have replaced the item.

P301.title: Media file missing
P301.message: The media file is missing from disk
P301.meaning: The item is in the library but its file is gone. It was moved, renamed or deleted, or the drive is not mounted.
P301.fix: Check the drive is mounted, then rescan the library.

P302.title: Media file unreadable
P302.message: The media file could not be read
P302.meaning: Reading the file failed. Usually a disconnected drive (EIO), a permissions problem, or a corrupt file.
P302.fix: See P201/P202 for drive and permission problems. Check Admin → Logs for the underlying error.

P303.title: ffmpeg not available
P303.message: Video conversion is unavailable: ffmpeg could not be started
P303.meaning: ffmpeg or ffprobe is missing or failed to launch, so videos that need converting cannot play.
P303.fix: The Docker image includes ffmpeg. On a bare-metal install, install ffmpeg and make sure it is on PATH. Check Admin → Logs.

P304.title: Conversion failed
P304.message: Converting this video failed on the server
P304.meaning: ffmpeg started but exited with an error while converting the video. Usually a corrupt file, an unsupported codec, or a hardware transcoding problem.
P304.fix: Admin → Logs shows the ffmpeg error. If it mentions VAAPI/QSV/NVENC, turn hardware transcoding off in Admin → Playback and try again.

P305.title: Still preparing
P305.message: Still preparing this video, try again shortly
P305.meaning: The conversion is running but has not produced the requested part yet.
P305.fix: The player retries this on its own. If it never finishes, the server may be too slow for real-time transcoding at this quality. Pick a lower quality.

P306.title: Invalid stream request
P306.meaning: The stream URL named an unknown quality, audio track, segment or preview sheet.
P306.fix: Reload the player. This usually means a stale URL after the video was rescanned.

P307.title: Subtitle track not found
P307.meaning: The requested subtitle track does not exist or could not be extracted.
P307.fix: Pick another track. Image-based subtitles (PGS/VobSub) cannot be shown as text.

P308.title: PDF reader not available
P308.message: PDF pages cannot be shown: poppler is not installed on the server
P308.meaning: Plinthio turns PDF pages into images with poppler (pdftoppm and pdfinfo), and it could not start them.
P308.fix: The Docker image includes poppler. On a bare-metal install, install poppler-utils (apt install poppler-utils, brew install poppler) and restart.

P309.title: PDF page could not be rendered
P309.message: This PDF page could not be rendered
P309.meaning: poppler started but failed on this file. Usually a damaged or password-protected PDF.
P309.fix: Open the file in another PDF reader to check it. A password-protected PDF has to be unlocked first. Admin → Logs has the error.

P350.title: Browser cannot play this format
P350.message: This browser cannot play this video
P350.meaning: The browser rejected the stream even after the server converted it.
P350.fix: Try another browser (Chrome, Edge or Safari). If this happens on every browser, the file itself may be damaged.

P351.title: Connection lost during playback
P351.meaning: The player could not reach the server to load the next part of the video.
P351.fix: Check your network connection, then press Retry.

P352.title: Media link could not be renewed
P352.message: Your media access expired and could not be renewed
P352.meaning: Media URLs carry a short-lived token. It expired and the app could not get a new one.
P352.fix: Reload the page. If that does not help, sign out and back in.

P400.title: TMDB key not configured
P400.message: TMDB API key is not configured. An admin must add one in Admin → Metadata.
P400.meaning: Movie, show and anime metadata comes from TMDB, which needs an API key. Release images have one built in; you see this on a build from source, or if TMDB stopped accepting the built-in key.
P400.fix: Create a key at themoviedb.org → Settings → API and paste it into Admin → Metadata.

P401.title: Provider rejected the API key
P401.message: The metadata provider rejected the configured API key
P401.meaning: The server reached the provider, but the provider refused the key.
P401.fix: For TMDB, paste either the "API Key" or the "API Read Access Token" from your TMDB account into Admin → Metadata.

P402.title: Provider rate limit
P402.message: The metadata provider is rate limiting this server. Wait a moment and try again.
P402.meaning: The provider is refusing requests because too many were sent.
P402.fix: Wait a minute. Batch matching large libraries can trigger this.

P403.title: Provider unreachable
P403.message: Could not reach the metadata provider from the server
P403.meaning: The request to the provider timed out or failed at the network level.
P403.fix: Check the server (container) has outbound internet access and DNS.

P404.title: Metadata source turned off
P404.message: This metadata source is turned off in Admin → Metadata.
P404.meaning: An admin switched off the only source for this kind of title, so it is not searched or matched.
P404.fix: Turn the source back on in Admin → Metadata → Sources, or fill the details in by hand.

P500.title: List not found
P500.meaning: The list or folder does not exist or belongs to someone else.

P501.title: Wrong kind of title for this list
P501.message: That kind of title cannot go in this list
P501.meaning: Each list holds one category: Movies, Shows, Anime, Read or Listen.
P501.fix: Add it to a list in the matching category.

P502.title: Already in list
P502.message: That title is already in this list
P502.meaning: The title was added to this list before.

P503.title: Already requested
P503.message: That title has already been requested
P503.meaning: Someone has an open request for this title.
P503.fix: Its status is shown on the Requests page.

P504.title: Already in the library
P504.message: That title has already been added to the library
P504.meaning: A request for this title was accepted and marked as added.

P505.title: Request can no longer be withdrawn
P505.message: Only pending requests can be withdrawn
P505.meaning: An admin or editor has already acted on this request.
P505.fix: Ask an admin or editor if you want it removed.

P506.title: Request not found
P506.meaning: The request was deleted or never existed.

P600.title: Watch parties are turned off
P600.message: Watch parties are turned off on this server
P600.meaning: An admin has not enabled watch parties.
P600.fix: An admin can turn them on in Admin → Features → Watch parties.

P601.title: Party not found
P601.message: That watch party has ended or never existed
P601.meaning: The host ended the party, everyone left, or the server restarted.
P601.fix: Ask the host for a new invite link.

P602.title: Only the host can do that
P602.message: Only the party host can do that
P602.meaning: The host has kept playback controls to themselves.
P602.fix: Ask the host, or ask them to let everyone control playback.

P603.title: Not available to your account
P603.message: This party is watching something your account can't open
P603.meaning: The title is hidden from you, or above your account's content limit.
P603.fix: Ask an admin about your account's content settings.

P604.title: Not everyone can watch that
P604.message: Someone in the party can't open that title
P604.meaning: The title is hidden from, or above the content limit of, someone watching.
P604.fix: Pick something everyone in the party can watch.

P605.title: Party is full
P605.meaning: A party holds up to 20 people, and a server runs up to 20 parties at once.
P605.fix: Try again when someone leaves or a party ends.

P700.title: Live TV is turned off
P700.message: Live TV is turned off on this server
P700.meaning: An admin has not turned on Live TV, or has turned it off.
P700.fix: An admin can turn it on in Admin → Live TV.

P701.title: Channel unavailable
P701.message: This channel could not be played right now
P701.meaning: The channel's stream did not answer, answered with an error, or points somewhere Plinthio will not connect to. Channels from public sources go offline or change address, and some only play in certain countries.
P701.fix: Try another channel, or try again later. An admin can refresh the source in Admin → Live TV, or hide channels that stay offline.

P702.title: Source could not be loaded
P702.message: The channel list could not be loaded
P702.meaning: Plinthio could not download or read a playlist, a programme guide, or the list of public channel presets.
P702.fix: Check the server can reach the internet (or the playlist's address), then try again. Admin → Live TV shows each source's last error.
